findings.reason: The eight Bruhat covers and their equivalence to nonzero mu-coefficient support are central data of this small-rank example. A four-level Hasse diagram materially exposes the two-by-two middle cover structure otherwise encoded in a long parenthesized list, while leaving the independent algebraic verification intact.
findings.action: Appended final Remarks with a six-permutation, eight-arrow TikZ Hasse diagram, inversion-length column and explicit crossing convention.

correction: Added only final Remarks illustrating the S3 Bruhat covers and hence mu=1 support. Original item bytes are an exact prefix of the current carrier.

diagram_math_checks.result: The six nodes are exactly S3 in one-line notation. Direct inversion counts give ranks {123}:0, {132,213}:1, {231,312}:2, {321}:3, matching item F6 and verification step 2.1. The right column aligns each displayed length with its node layer.

Independently enumerated reduced subwords using 132=s2, 213=s1, 231=s1s2, 312=s2s1, 321=s1s2s1. The reduced-subword criterion of F6 gives exactly the eight length-one pairs 123->132, 123->213, 132->231, 132->312, 213->231, 213->312, 231->321, 312->321. Script parses TikZ edges and checks exact equality to those pairs. No transitive noncover edge is drawn.

Step 1.3 gives coefficients p_y,w=v^(ell(w)-ell(y)) for all comparable pairs. F4 and the local q-normalization definition identify mu(y,w) with [v]p_y,w, so it equals one precisely for those eight comparable length-one pairs; larger gaps give zero. Thus each arrow and the exact-support caption match step 2.1.

All eight arrows point from the lower inversion-length node to the higher one. The two middle diagonals intersect only geometrically; the caption explicitly states the crossing is not a vertex, so it introduces neither a seventh permutation nor an extra order relation.
All original Facts, Example and five Verification steps are preserved byte-for-byte; the diagram follows the final QED in a separate Remarks section. It supplies no premise to the proof.
